name: Backpack
description: A rugged leather pack with worn straps, favored by travelers to carry provisions and gear across long roads.

name: Barrel
description: A stout wooden barrel bound in iron hoops, ideal for storing ale, salted meat, or contraband in dim taverns and cellars.

name: Cask
description: A small oak cask, its aroma hinting at strong spirits within, prized by innkeepers and travelers alike.

name: Flask
description: A slim metal flask, perfect for concealing strong drink or potions beneath a cloak.

name: Jug
description: A simple clay jug, sturdy and well-used, often found on farmhouse tables or in bustling markets.

name: Pewter Stein
description: A heavy pewter stein, etched with crude motifs, clinks loudly in rowdy tavern halls.

name: Pouch
description: A small leather pouch, perfect for hiding coins or trinkets at a belt or beneath a cloak.

name: Sack
description: A coarse burlap sack, smelling faintly of grain and soil, slung across farmyards or market stalls.

name: Large Sack
description: A broad burlap sack capable of holding heavy loads, often bulging with goods on market days.

name: Saddlebags
description: A pair of weathered leather saddlebags, stained with dust and road grime from countless journeys.

name: Sling Bag
description: A simple cloth sling bag, favored by common folk for carrying daily necessities.

name: Scroll Case
description: A polished leather scroll case with brass fittings, used to safeguard fragile writings from dust and rain.

name: Waterskin
description: A leather waterskin with a cork stopper, indispensable for travelers braving long roads or dry wastes.
